summary: Applies METHODOLOGY.md decision 16 to the St Kitts and Nevis audit reports 2018-2022: 8 rows of capital budget additions and audited spending on the Hurricane Relief Programme, under a proposed indicator cbi_option_financed_spending, each noting that the reports do not trace which money came from CBI. The option's proceeds (Hurricane Relief Fund fees collected by the CIU) were already recorded for 2018, 2019, 2021 and 2022; 2020 prints no split; no report prints a balance of the fund.

observations.location: PDF p. 29 (printed p. 20), Capital Expenditure, budget revisions
observations.notes: Federal Government of St. Kitts only (excludes Nevis Island Administration). One of four projects for which the 2018 capital budget was revised from $147 million to $294 million; the report says the project was not budgeted for in 2018. The four listed amounts (0.342 + 38 + 97 + 11 = 293.3) plus the approved $147 million come to 293.3 against the printed revised $294 million, so the list does not reconcile exactly (rounded amounts; the report does not say the list is complete). The report does not say how this spending was financed and does not trace which money came from CBI: it reports fees collected for the Hurricane Relief Fund (a CBI contribution option) as Citizenship by Investment Unit revenue, but it does not link those receipts to this capital project. Recorded under METHODOLOGY.md decision 16; never add to CBI spending totals. Printed as a bare '$'; recorded as Eastern Caribbean dollars, the currency of the issuing government (METHODOLOGY.md decision 5).

new_indicators.name: Spending on a programme financed through a CBI option
new_indicators.definition: Government spending (budgeted or actual, as printed) on a programme that a CBI investment option finances, such as St Kitts and Nevis' Hurricane Relief Programme, financed by the Hurricane Relief Fund option whose proceeds were collected as CIU revenue. Breakdown category= for the programme (e.g. hurricane_relief_programme) and item= where the report lists projects. Recorded as printed; the source usually does not trace which money came from CBI. Never added to CBI spending totals (METHODOLOGY.md decision 16).
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-kna-hurricane-2026-10-10 under METHODOLOGY.md decision 16. Not the same as cbi_fund_payments (payments out of a CBI fund itself) or cbi_programme_costs (costs of running the programme).

gaps: No report 2018-2022 prints a balance or cumulative total of the Hurricane Relief Fund, or says which receipts paid for the Hurricane Relief Programme.
2019 lists the Hurricane Relief Programme among capital budget additions without an amount; 2020 prints no split of CIU collections, so no Hurricane Relief Fund collection for 2020.

ledger.contains: Audit report on the 2018 public accounts. Programme content: CIU collected $418 million (recorded) = government fees $78m + Hurricane Relief Fund $242m + Sustainable Growth Fund $2m + application fees $8m + background checks $88m (components now recorded; they add up to 418); CIU 46% of recurrent revenue (recorded) and 32% of operating cash receipts (recorded); appropriation warrants for CBI consultancy and operating costs in Q4 2018 ($56m) and CIU marketing fees ($14m) (recorded). Hurricane Relief Programme (financed through the CBI Hurricane Relief Fund option; METHODOLOGY.md decision 16): $38 million added to the 2018 capital budget and $38 million spent (recorded as cbi_option_financed_spending, with a note that the report does not trace which money came from CBI). Not recorded: 'The initial budget allocation of $2.5 million was revised to $41 million' (PDF p. 30), which most likely is the Office of the Prime Minister's whole capital allocation (the report says the programme was not budgeted for in 2018). No balance of the Hurricane Relief Fund is printed. Year-on-year changes and variances against the revenue projection are printed but not recorded (derived comparisons; the projection itself is not printed). Not recorded: a $10 million warrant for the SIDF (government money paid to the foundation, not CBI receipts). Out of scope: other departments' revenue, taxes, expenditure, debt, deposit accounts and the special audits.

Audit report on the 2019 public accounts. Programme content: CIU collected almost $443 million (recorded) = government fees $168m + Hurricane Relief Fund $139m + Sustainable Growth Fund $78m + application fees $12m + background checks $46m (components now recorded; they add up to 443); CIU 45% of recurrent revenue (recorded) and 36% of operating cash receipts (recorded). No CBI items among the 2019 appropriation warrants. Hurricane Relief Programme (decision 16): listed among unbudgeted capital additions with no amount (no row), $17 million spent (recorded as cbi_option_financed_spending, with a note that the report does not trace which money came from CBI). No balance of the Hurricane Relief Fund is printed. Year-on-year changes and variances against the revenue projection are printed but not recorded (derived comparisons; the projection itself is not printed). Out of scope: other departments' revenue, taxes, expenditure, debt, deposit accounts and the special audits.

Audit report on the 2020 public accounts. Programme content: CIU collected $270 million (recorded), 40% of recurrent revenue (recorded); no split by component is given this year; appropriation warrant of $25 million for CBI due diligence consultancy and operating costs (recorded). Hurricane Relief Programme (decision 16): $3 million added for suppliers and contractors and $8 million spent (recorded as cbi_option_financed_spending, with a note that the report does not trace which money came from CBI). No Hurricane Relief Fund collection or balance is printed this year. Year-on-year changes and variances against the revenue projection are printed but not recorded (derived comparisons; the projection itself is not printed). Out of scope: other departments' revenue, taxes, expenditure, debt, deposit accounts and the special audits.

Audit report on the 2021 public accounts. Programme content: CIU collected $543 million (recorded) = government fees $278m + Hurricane Relief Fund $333 thousand + Sustainable Growth Fund $123m + application fees $27m + background checks $114m (components now recorded; sum 542.3, within rounding of 543); CIU 57% of recurrent revenue (recorded); appropriation warrant of $18 million for due diligence and CIU expenses (recorded). Hurricane Relief Programme (decision 16): $2 million spent (recorded as cbi_option_financed_spending, with a note that the report does not trace which money came from CBI). No balance of the Hurricane Relief Fund is printed. Year-on-year changes and variances against the revenue projection are printed but not recorded (derived comparisons; the projection itself is not printed). Not recorded: $60 million owed by public bodies to the SIDF and not being repaid (public debt, PDF p. 42). Out of scope: other departments' revenue, taxes, expenditure, debt, deposit accounts and the special audits.

Audit report on the 2022 public accounts. Programme content: CIU collected $669 million (recorded) = government fees $343m + Hurricane Relief Fund $376 thousand + Sustainable Growth Fund $123m + application fees $29m + background checks $174m (components now recorded; sum 669.4); CIU 60% of recurrent revenue (recorded); CBI dividend: $19 million added to the capital budget for two disbursements, $19 million spent, and over $14.8 million actually paid out by the Social Security Board for the December 2022 payout by August 2023 (all recorded). Hurricane Relief Programme (decision 16): $991 thousand added for contractors and suppliers and $2 million spent (recorded as cbi_option_financed_spending, with a note that the report does not trace which money came from CBI). No balance of the Hurricane Relief Fund is printed. Year-on-year changes and variances against the revenue projection are printed but not recorded (derived comparisons; the projection itself is not printed). Not recorded: a $31 million warrant that mixes CBI due diligence with other Office of the Prime Minister expenses and an extra month's salary (PDF p. 27; not a programme-only amount); $27.7 million owed to the SIDF (public debt, PDF p. 44). Out of scope: other departments' revenue, taxes, expenditure, debt, deposit accounts and the special audits.
